title: Quantized run governance: scheduling, TTL and access controls for calibration artifacts
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Goal: Provide a clear orchestration model in Redwood Console for quantization calibration runs (FP8/INT8) focusing on scheduling/execution controls, artifact TTL/retention policies, run-level access controls, and deterministic accuracy validation. This ticket scopes the product & UX requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout constraints for run governance features that enable teams to safely run wide calibration sweeps and keep artifact storage under control while preserving auditability and reproducibility.

Problem context: Calibration jobs produce model artifacts (quant profiles, calibration traces, histogram artifacts) that can be large and numerous when performing parameter sweeps. Customers need: efficient scheduling, predictable storage costs (TTL/retention tiers), immutable signed artifacts for deployment, and per-run access controls so security-sensitive teams can restrict who can view/delete artifacts. Additionally, calibration runs must integrate with the accuracy validation pipeline so a failed regression triggers notifications and optional auto-revert of rollout candidates.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- Run lifecycle controls in Console: schedule (immediate / queued / cron / ad-hoc sweep), pause/resume, cancel, retry.
- Artifact retention policies: default TTLs, manual pin/lock for important artifacts, tiered retention (hot/archival), and automated cleanup jobs.
- Run-level RBAC: role-based visibility (viewer/operator/owner) and delete permissions; integration with org-wide SSO/SAML groups.
- Signed immutable artifacts with content-hash lineage metadata and linkage to the calibration input dataset/hash and evaluation metrics.
- Integration hooks for accuracy validation: preflight tests, post-run regression checks, alerting destinations, and optional auto-rollback triggers if regression crosses threshold.
- Cost guardrails: run budget caps, notifications on projected storage/cpu/GPU cost for a sweep.

Out of scope: low-level runtime kernel optimizations, per-kernel trace capture formats, and on-prem install mechanics (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: Users can create a calibration run with scheduling options (immediate/queued/cron) and specify TTL/retention tier
Retention engine: System automatically deletes artifacts after TTL unless artifact is pinned - deletion runs are logged and reversible within a 24h grace window
RBAC: Run creator can grant/revoke viewer/operator/owner roles; delete action requires owner role and logs an audit event
Signed artifacts: Every quant profile artifact stored has a content-hash and signature; download includes lineage (model version, dataset hash, run id)

Accuracy validation: Post-run validation pipeline runs automatically and writes pass/fail plus metric diffs; if regression > configured threshold, a notification is posted and an optional auto-revert flag can be enabled
Cost guardrails: Users can set a run budget and the system warns when projected spend for queued sweep exceeds budget
APIs: All run controls and artifact operations are available via Redwood API with equivalent permissions
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff with Eng (Diego, Lin), Design (Maya). Agreed product boundaries and list of critical UX states (create, monitor, pin, cleanup).
2025-02-21: Eng raised a concern about supporting cron schedules for large sweeps; suggested a queued backpressure model instead to protect Dedicated GPU pools.
2025-02-25: Design proposed a compact run-card UI to surface TTL, pinned state, budget, and validation status. Shared initial mock in Figma: /drive/redwood/figma/quant-run-card
2025-03-01: Security reviewed artifact signing proposal; requested HSM/KMS integration notes and audit event schema. Added security_review_required flag.
2025-03-04: PM decision: implement queued scheduling (cron via queued trigger that enqueues runs) to reduce scheduler complexity; include explicit scheduled-run window and throttling controls.
review_feedback: Design feedback (Maya): clarify pinned artifact UX so users don't accidentally unpin and lose provenance; add explicit warnings before pin removal.
Eng feedback (Lin): prefer a separate cleanup microservice to own TTL enforcement and to emit deletion events for traceability.
Security feedback (Avery): require KMS-backed signatures and retention of signature verification logs for 90 days for compliance customers.
tradeoffs: Full cron scheduling vs queued-only: Chosen queued model reduces load on runtime and allows centralized backpressure; sacrifice convenience of arbitrary cron windows in v1.
Immediate hard delete vs grace window: Implemented 24h reversible grace window to protect against operator error at the cost of slightly more storage retention.
Per-run immutability vs edit-in-place metadata: Artifacts immutable after creation; metadata (tags/notes) editable - preserves reproducibility but requires additional metadata index.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large sweeps could exhaust artifact storage - Mitigation: enforce per-run budget and automatic estimated-cost warnings before run enqueue; require explicit approval for runs over threshold.
Risk: Unauthorized deletion - Mitigation: RBAC plus audit logs and 24h grace window for deletions; alerting on mass-deletion events.
Risk: False negatives in accuracy validation pipeline - Mitigation: run a small sample of golden prompts as preflight and keep versioned eval test-suite with guardrails.
next_steps: Confirm API contract with Eng (open RFC) and add to ENG-2042
Design: finalize run-card and artifact details; add empty-state and error states
Security: define KMS integration SLOs and logging schema
PM: prepare release notes and migration plan for existing calibration artifacts
Schedule spike for cleanup microservice and cost projection calculations
